output.name: Tekma
output.myth: Tekma nests on the high ledge above the landing, where the rock is wet and gives under a hand. She is grey and heavy with fish, and she keeps her oil in her gut the way a wife keeps salt in a jar. Once Aun, who was young and had more rope than sense, climbed past her ledge to see what lay over the top. Tekma turned and spat her oil into his hair. It stank for a month. Aun laughed, which is why he never learned to be sorry. Tavo, watching from the wind, laughed too and tried to blow the stink away, but it would not go. When Aun cut the string and the sky drifted off, Tekma went up with the other kites, and she is still up there in the Reach. So when a child goes up the cliff, the old ones say: mind Tekma. She has not forgotten Aun, and she will not forget you.
output.verse:
Oil on the cliff-edge,
she spits warm oil at the climb.
Turn back, fool, and live.
